source.title: MISTRA Coalitions Barometer Dataset, 2026 edition
source.attribution: Caromba, L., Simayile, S., & Ndletyana, A. (2026). MISTRA Coalitions Barometer Dataset, 2026 edition (Version 1.0) [Data set]. Mapungubwe Institute for Strategic Reflection. https://coalitions.mistra.org.za
source.licence: CC BY 4.0 for original MISTRA coding. Underlying IEC seats and municipal identifiers retain their original terms.
source.modifications: Dates normalised; municipal codes matched to Counted IDs; party labels expanded; release-note issues attached. Sourced Counted clarifications are marked editorialCorrection, which retains the original notes and any changed termination code. Inaugural values retained.
source.basis: Party roles, seats and officeholders describe inauguration. Later changes may appear only in notes. Active means active at the source cutoff, not today.
source.coverage: 175 administrations in 80 local and metropolitan municipalities. Districts are excluded. Missing coverage does not mean no coalition.

records.notes: Speaker N. P. Yantolo-Nkonyeni was replaced by E. A. Miggels of the EFF, the party's only councillor. The date on which this occurred could not be established.

Mayor F. J. Yake's surname is spelled Yakhe in the ANC's own announcement of his candidacy. By-elections in September and November 2025 moved two ANC seats to the PA. This took this coalition from the seven seats recorded here to five out of twelve, below a majority. Speaker D. Maasdorp was removed by a council vote in December 2025, and S. Ferguson of the FF Plus became acting speaker.

Mayor S. Ngodwana was removed by a council vote in March 2024, the coalition's smaller partners voting with an opposition motion. Two sittings then failed to elect a successor, and the province warned it would consider intervening. N. Xhakaza of the ANC was elected in April.
issues: Release note: transition should be Reshuffling, not Reduction.

records.notes: The mayor and deputy mayor were elected by secret ballot, so the vote carries no party attribution. Seventeen smaller parties are coded Unknown on that account.
Al Jama-ah, the DLC and the MSA each voted with the government once and were absent when it was next tested; KZNI voted with it once and against it once. All four are coded Unknown.
The MSA voted with the government at the one confidence division held in this period and is recorded at no other. It is coded Unknown.
issues: Release note: ideological classification conflicts with coded membership.

records.notes: Mayor N. Ntema was removed from office by a council vote in April 2025 and an acting mayor was elected at the same sitting. No authoritative source naming that person was found.
Mayor M. Mosia-Lakaje was recalled by the ANC and resigned in June 2024. M. Melato of the ANC was elected mayor in her place.
The FF Plus joined the mayoral committee in about July 2023, after this administration formed. The role cells record the relationships at formation.

Mayor D. Thupane resigned in October 2024 and L. G. Sele of the ANC, the sitting speaker, was elected mayor. D. David of the ANC became speaker. An IFP councillor took the new post of deputy executive mayor in November 2024.

Mayor G. Khoza resigned in October 2023 and W. M. Matsheke, also of the ANC, was elected in her place. N. Molatlhegi was elected to the new post of deputy executive mayor on 1 December 2023. S. Moumakwe was elected speaker on 1 December 2023.
This administration lasted under a month, too short for several parties to be observed in a role. The AIC, ATM, PAC and UDM are all coded as Unknown.
Mayor T. Amad resigned in April 2023 and K. Gwamanda of Al Jama-ah was elected eleven days later. A June 2023 by-election moved a seat from the ANC to the PA.
issues: Release note: AHC is coded as opposition but a cited source lists it as a member.

records.notes: Speaker N. Mthembu was removed by a council vote in June 2025 and M. Arnolds of the AIC was elected in her place the following month. The council created the city's first deputy mayor post in January 2026. Masuku was elected to it on 26 February 2026.
Mayor S. Khathi resigned to take a provincial post and Deputy Mayor M. Mbutho acted from September 2023. A July 2022 by-election moved a seat from the DA to the ANC.
A by-election in October 2022 moved a seat from Al Jama-ah to the IFP during this administration, taking the IFP from five seats to six.

The Coalitions Barometer 2021-2023 describes an ANC support bloc without naming its members, so the ABC, ACDP, AIC, JEP, PA and the independent councillor are coded Unknown. Ward 2 moved to the IFP in March 2023 and back to the ANC in December 2024.
A by-election in June 2023 moved a seat from the IFP to the ANC during this administration, taking the IFP and DA together below the votes needed to carry a motion.
The ABC withdrew from this administration in April 2023 on a directive from its president, P. Mavundla. The administration continued without it.
Mayor S. Ndlovu resigned in November 2024 after the DA filed a no-confidence motion, and M. Mkhize, also of the IFP, was elected later that month.
A by-election in June 2023 moved a seat from the ANC to the IFP during this administration, taking the IFP to ten seats and the ANC to nine.

A by-election in June 2024 moved a seat from the ABC to the IFP during this administration, taking the IFP to eleven seats and the ABC to six. The ANC's provincial leadership directed its councillors to break with the IFP in October 2025. No withdrawal was completed and the ANC speaker continued to convene the council.
The EFF withdrew its support at the end of January 2023 after an announcement by J. Malema, and this administration continued without it. By-elections during 2024 moved seats from the ANC to the IFP.
Speaker M. J. Mthethwa resigned from the office in early 2023, while remaining a councillor. P. X. Qwabe was speaker by 30 June 2023.
During this period, a by-election in March 2023 replaced an independent councillor with one from the IFP, taking the IFP from eight seats to nine.
issues: Release note: deputy mayor vacancy date conflicts with a financial statement.

records.notes: Speaker S. Myaka was removed by a council vote in December 2024 and S. Ndlela of the IFP, an opposition party, was elected in his place. No new administration followed, and an office won against one does not make its holder a partner.
The ABC, the CFP and the DA are coded Unknown. The motion that formed this administration needed at least four votes beyond the IFP's nine, and no source was found recording how any party voted.
Some sources name the deputy mayor, S. J. Kunene, as Majuba Mavuso.
Mayor M. Maphisa was suspended in February 2023, and was recalled by the IFP the following month.
By-elections in February 2022 moved a seat from the IFP to the NFP during this administration, taking the IFP to twenty seats and the NFP to fourteen.
A by-election in February 2026 took a seat from the NFP to the IFP.
Deputy Mayor M. Z. Mhlongo resigned on 2 June 2022 and E. Z. Mtshali was appointed in his place the same day.
By-elections in April 2023 and February 2025 each moved a seat from the ANC to the IFP during this administration, taking the IFP to seventeen seats and the ANC to sixteen.
A by-election in January 2023 caused a seat to switch from the ANC to the IFP during this administration, taking the IFP from nineteen seats to twenty.

A by-election in February 2023 moved a second seat from the ANC to the IFP during this administration, taking the IFP from twenty seats to twenty-one. N. Mthethwa (EFF) was deputy mayor in February 2023, when the EFF instructed its deputy mayors to resign. M. Z. Shobede was deputy mayor at 30 June 2024.

A by-election in September 2022 moved a seat from the ANC to the IFP during this administration, taking the IFP from twenty-three seats to twenty-four. Mayor N. Dando resigned two weeks after taking office and X. Ngwezi, also of the IFP, was elected in December 2021.
The Coalitions Barometer 2021-2023 names the blocs on either side of this council, but does not place the NFP in either of them. It is therefore coded as Unknown.
The Coalitions Barometer 2023-2025 is silent on the NFP's role while other sources list it as a member, so the NFP is coded Unknown. A September 2023 by-election moved a seat from the ANC to the IFP.
Mayor L. Nhaca was removed by a council vote in October 2024. M. A. Ngidi of the ANC was elected mayor days later, with N. Cele as deputy mayor.
Speaker D. Msibi resigned in June 2025 and P. Mahlaba was elected in his place. Mahlaba's party could not be established.
The EFF opposed this administration when it formed, but switched over to supporting it during the term. The role cells record the relationships at formation.
Speaker T. Mpye resigned the chair in August 2023 while remaining a councillor. He co-sponsored a motion against Mayor P. M. Masilela.

A by-election in May 2025 moved a seat from the NCM to the ANC during this administration, leaving the DA and NCM together one short of a majority. Mayor G. Bock and Speaker R. Kritzinger exchanged offices in June 2024 under a rotation agreed between the NCM and the DA in 2021.

A by-election in December 2024 caused a seat to shift from the DA to the ANC during this administration, giving the ANC six of eleven seats and a majority on its own. The termination reason is the most likely event on the available evidence: no record shows whether the council removed the mayor in December 2024 by a motion of no confidence.
This administration lasted sixteen days and no council sitting fell inside it, so the DA, PA and FF Plus are all coded Unknown.
The FF Plus was given the speakership when this administration formed, which rules out opposition but does not show whether it governed as a partner or supported from outside. It is coded Unknown.
No minute or report of the installation vote was found, but the DA's two seats could not have carried it alone. The ANC, PA and FF Plus are all coded Unknown.
A by-election in June 2022 took a seat from the ANC to the DA, lifting this administration one seat above a majority. Some sources give the speaker's initials as D. S. Malgas.
Mayor L. Makenna and Speaker D. Jonas were removed by a council vote in December 2021, and a court set that vote aside and returned both in January 2022.

issues: Release note: inaugural mayor is coded Unknown despite a named source.
Release note: conflicting start dates; inaugural mayor is coded Unknown despite a named source.

records.notes: A by-election in October 2024 moved a seat from the DA to the ANC during this administration, giving the ANC six of eleven seats. The DA and COPE continued to govern for another 47 days.

issues: Release note: inaugural mayor is coded Unknown despite a named source.

records.notes: Mayor K. D. Sonyoni and Speaker N. N. Maputle were both recalled in December 2024. M. Bartlett and D. Peters, both of the ANC, were elected in their places.
Mayor T. B. Afrika was replaced by W. Harmse, also of the ANC. Neither the exact date on which this occurred nor the reason why it happened could be established.
Some sources spell the speaker's surname Lekgadi.
The mayor recorded here was elected in October 2023, when the sittings that installed this administration were repeated. The name of the councillor installed in August could not be found.
issues: Release note: named mayor took office after the administration began; inaugural mayor is uncertain.

records.notes: In October 2024 Mayor G. van Niekerk and Deputy Mayor B. Lobishe resigned and were each elected to the other's office.

The motion that formed this administration carried without objection and the mayor was elected unopposed, so no vote was recorded by party. The ANC is coded Unknown. Speaker R. Matlholoa held the office in an acting capacity. J. Modisakeng was in the chair by January 2025, and neither the date of the change nor his party could be established.

In September 2025 the existing council elected a new mayor and speaker under national intervention. The council was not dissolved. This corrects the source’s termination code to agree with its own narrative.

editorialCorrection.originalNotes: This administration ended in September 2025 when the council elected a new mayor and speaker under a national intervention. The termination value names dissolution, but the council was not dissolved and stayed in place.

records.notes: The council combines the offices of mayor and speaker in one councillor.

M. Makwarela left the speakership to take the mayoralty, so the speakership is recorded as Vacant. This administration lasted ten days, too short to observe the PA, AIC and RCoT, which are coded Unknown.

issues: Release note: conflicting start dates; inaugural mayor is coded Unknown despite a named source.

records.notes: The PA's ward councillor left for the DA in May 2022, leaving the DA and FF Plus one short of a majority on the seven seats recorded here. A July by-election gave the DA the seat and the majority.
issues: Release note: inaugural mayor is coded Unknown despite a named source.

records.notes: By-elections in April and August 2024 moved two ANC seats, one to the CFRA and one to the DA, taking this administration from the six it needed for a majority to eight.
Mayor R. Richards resigned in June 2025 and A. Scheepers of the ANC was elected. Scheepers had already replaced A. Mouton as deputy mayor earlier that year.
The deputy mayoralty was vacant at formation, and C. Laubscher of the DA filled it five weeks later. Mayor A. Truter stepped down at the end of January 2026.
Speaker J. Mouton was removed by a council vote in May 2022, and E. Sidego of the DA replaced him. Deputy Mayor K. Robyn gave way to F. Klazen of GOOD.

issues: Release note: LIP support has weak supporting evidence.

records.notes: Contemporaneous reporting places the EFF in conflict with this administration at its first sitting, and a later retrospective places it inside the founding coalition. Both Coalitions Barometer volumes leave it open, so the EFF is coded Unknown. Mayor K. Papier died in office in August 2023 and M. Liebenberg, also of the PA, was elected in his place in September.
S. Shuma was deputy executive mayor from August 2024, after the administration took office.

GOOD expelled its three councillors nine days after this administration formed, leaving the speakership vacant until November 2024. Mayor T. Zimmermann's surname is spelled Zimmerman in court judgments.
Mayor P. Swart was removed by a council vote in May 2024. Deputy Mayor R. Ross then acted in the office, and was elected mayor in June 2024.
One of the eleven seats was vacant when this administration formed. Speaker J. van Schalkwyk resigned his seat in February 2025 and J. du T. Loubser, also of the FF Plus, was elected in his place.
issues: Source party seats do not sum to the recorded council size (vacancies or incomplete allocation).

records.notes: The ANC withdrew from the coalition in December 2021 and directed its councillors to the opposition benches, keeping the speakership. It is coded Opposition.
issues: Release note: KIP membership has weak supporting evidence.

records.notes: Deputy Mayor W. Meshoa was replaced by Ruiters, also of ICOSA. The date on which this occurred could not be established.

The DA reached 28 of 55 seats after the July 2023 by-elections. That outright majority was temporary: it lost ward 8 to the PA in February 2024. The DA–FF+ coalition ended in June 2024. The source’s phrase “governed alone from then” should not be read as continuous single-party government for the rest of the term.

editorialCorrection.originalNotes: By-elections in July 2023 took the DA to twenty-eight of fifty-five seats, an outright majority, and it governed alone from then.

records.notes: Three of the fifty-five seats were vacant when this administration formed. All three were filled by by-elections in January and February 2026, and the Patriotic Alliance won all three.
issues: Source party seats do not sum to the recorded council size (vacancies or incomplete allocation).

records.notes: ICOSA left this administration in April 2022 when a council vote removed its deputy mayor, and L. Campher of AK was elected in his place.
Deputy Mayor M. Nyuka resigned in November 2022 and V. Donson of ICOSA was elected in his place. Both parties remained in the coalition.

Deputy Mayor A. Marbi of the PBI resigned in March 2025. Speaker M. Skosana was removed as a councillor in May 2025 and the speakership fell with his seat; M. Willemse of the Knysna Independent Movement replaced him.
The mayoralty changed twice inside this administration. M. J. Smith gave way to J. Botha of the ANC in 2022, and Botha to A. Kleinbooi of the PA in 2023.
Evidence of the ANC's relationship to this administration points different ways, and whether it is government or opposition could not be definitively established. The ANC is therefore coded Unknown.

Mayor G. Pietersen was replaced by T. Prince of the PA, who resigned on 31 January 2023. A. Sauls of the PA was elected mayor in February 2023. By-elections in June 2024 took the DA from four seats to seven of thirteen, an outright majority, which it then used the following month to vote this coalition out.

C. De Bruin was elected mayor seven votes to five, one councillor excused. Two votes came from DA councillors, and it could not be established which two of the PA, GOOD and KDF joined the ANC, so all three are coded Unknown. G. Duimpies, the deputy mayor, was acting mayor for about two months before her election as mayor in September 2025.
